ayas_yv_cell.caveat: The Yajurvedic ayas cell is a matcher miss, not a corpus absence. VSM 18.13 names ayas in its metals list, but the word stands there in its sandhi-elided form: after 'me' the initial a- elides to an avagraha, so the printed surface is avagraha+yas, and the search normalisation drops the avagraha and leaves the bare token 'yasca'. That token is indistinguishable from the relative pronoun yas and from the -ayas ca plural stems standing in the same line of the same verse -- girayasca 'and the mountains', parvatasca, vanaspatayasca. Registering an alias for it would manufacture false positives demonstrably inside the witness verse itself. The neighbouring metals in the same list ARE matched -- trapu, sisa, syama and loha each reach this verse -- which is what establishes the ayas miss as a matcher limitation rather than an absence.
ayas_yv_cell.why_no_alias_was_manufactured: Three reasons, each on record. (1) docs/architecture/RIGVEDA_LEXICAL_MENTION_POLICY.md:48-64 forbids substring and surface-form matching outright, for exactly the sandhi false-positive rate demonstrated here. (2) A sandhi-conditioned alias is a feature-conditioned alias over a corpus with no morphological annotation to condition on: GAP-MORPHOLOGY-002 records, with five-field blocker evidence, that no published morphological annotation exists for the Yajurveda. (3) Making the avagraha survive the fold would change the sealed search-normalisation contract for all four corpora, where over- and under-normalising both look like a clean run.
